annotation.cut_point:
We are given the set:

$$
S = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2020\}
$$

We are to **select $ n $ numbers from this set**, and then from those $ n $, **choose any two numbers $ a $ and $ b $ such that $ a $ does not divide $ b $**. We are to **maximize** $ n $, **under the condition that in the selected $ n $ numbers, there is at least one pair $ (a, b) $ with $ a \mid b $** (i.e., $ a $ divides $ b $).

verified_state: The problem asks to select n numbers so that any two selected numbers a and b satisfy that a does not divide b (i.e., the selected set is an antichain under divisibility).
reflection.error_step: We are to **maximize** $ n $, **under the condition that in the selected $ n $ numbers, there is at least one pair $ (a, b) $ with $ a \mid b $** (i.e., $ a $ divides $ b $).
reflection.error_reason: This reverses the required condition: the selected subset must have no divisibility relation among any chosen pair, not contain at least one divisible pair.
reflection.new_direction: Reinterpret the problem as maximizing a subset of {1,...,2020} with no element dividing another, then use the standard pairing of numbers by odd part to prove the upper bound.
